claim_verdicts.evidence: git-branch(1) 2.46: "The command's second form creates a new branch head named <branchname> which points to the current HEAD" and "Note that this will create the new branch, but it will not switch the working tree to it". gitglossary(7), head: "A named reference to the commit at the tip of a branch. Heads are stored in a file in $GIT_DIR/refs/heads/ directory, except when using packed refs." A ref file holds one id, so cost does not grow with project size.
claim_verdicts.source: C:/Program Files/Git/mingw64/share/doc/git-doc/git-branch.html:507-517; gitglossary.html:723-726 (Git for Windows v2.46.0 manual)

claim_verdicts.evidence: git-switch(1) 2.46 DESCRIPTION: "Switch to a specified branch. The working tree and the index are updated to match the branch. All new commits will be added to the tip of this branch." gitglossary(7), detached HEAD: "Normally the HEAD stores the name of a branch... However, Git also allows you to check out an arbitrary commit that isn't necessarily the tip of any particular branch. The HEAD in such a state is called 'detached'."

git-commit(1) 2.46 DESCRIPTION: "Create a new commit containing the current contents of the index and the given log message describing the changes. The new commit is a direct child of HEAD, usually the tip of the current branch, and the branch is updated to point to it (unless no branch is associated with the working tree, in which case HEAD is 'detached'...)". Only that branch is named as updated.

git-remote(1) 2.46, add: "Add a remote named <name> for the repository at <URL>. The command git fetch <name> can then be used to create and update remote-tracking branches <name>/<branch>." gitglossary(7), origin: "The default upstream repository. Most projects have at least one upstream project which they track. By default origin is used for that purpose."

gitglossary(7) 2.46, remote-tracking branch: "A ref that is used to follow changes from another repository. It typically looks like refs/remotes/foo/bar ... A remote-tracking branch should not contain direct modifications or have local commits made to it." git-remote(1) add: "git fetch <name> can then be used to create and update remote-tracking branches" — i.e. written by commands that contact the remote.

git-fetch(1) 2.46 DESCRIPTION: "Fetch branches and/or tags (collectively, 'refs') from one or more other repositories, along with the objects necessary to complete their histories. Remote-tracking branches are updated" — nothing else is said to change. git-pull(1): "More precisely, git pull runs git fetch with the given parameters and then depending on configuration options or command line flags, will call either git rebase or git merge to reconcile diverging branches."
git-push(1) 2.46 DESCRIPTION: "Updates remote refs using local refs, while sending objects necessary to complete the given refs."

git-pull(1) 2.46: "Incorporates changes from a remote repository into the current branch... If the current branch and the remote have diverged, the user needs to specify how to reconcile the divergent branches with --rebase or --no-rebase"; "git pull runs git fetch ... then ... will call either git rebase or git merge"; and "See git-merge(1) for details, including how conflicts are presented and handled" / "to cancel a conflicting merge, use git reset --merge" — i.e. the second step can stop part-way.

git-clone(1) 2.46, --bare: "Make a bare Git repository. That is, instead of creating <directory> and placing the administrative files in <directory>/.git, make the <directory> itself the $GIT_DIR. This obviously implies the --no-checkout because there is nowhere to check out the working tree." gitglossary(7), bare repository: "Usually publishers of public repositories make bare repositories available."

git-clone(1) 2.46, --bare: "the branch heads at the remote are copied directly to corresponding local branch heads". git-fetch(1), CONFIGURED REMOTE-TRACKING BRANCHES: "The example above will fetch all branches that exist in the origin (i.e. any ref that matches the left-hand side of the value, refs/heads/*) and update the corresponding remote-tracking branches in the refs/remotes/origin/* hierarchy." Captured run shows origin/feature/currency and origin/feature/shipping.

git-branch(1) 2.46: "-u <upstream> / --set-upstream-to=<upstream>: Set up <branchname>'s tracking information so <upstream> is considered <branchname>'s upstream branch." git-status(1): "--ahead-behind ... Display or do not display detailed ahead/behind counts for the branch relative to its upstream branch. Defaults to true." The count is computed from refs already in the repository, no remote contact.

git-branch(1) 2.46: "existing branches are listed; the current branch will be highlighted in green and marked with an asterisk"; "-v/-vv/--verbose: When in list mode, show sha1 and commit subject line for each head, along with relationship to upstream branch (if any). If given twice, print ... the name of the upstream branch, as well". Captured run line 4: "* main             57a2d53 [origin/main] Add a README".

git-log(1) 2.46: "--graph: Draw a text-based graphical representation of the commit history on the left hand side of the output."; "--decorate: Print out the ref names of any commits that are shown"; "--all: Pretend as if all the refs in refs/, along with HEAD, are listed on the command line". Captured run lines 7-17 show the `*`, the round brackets, the `|` columns and the `|/` lines.

git-rev-parse(1) 2.46: "--abbrev-ref[=(strict|loose)]: A non-ambiguous short name of the objects name." The documentation alone does not say HEAD resolves to the branch name, but the captured run settles it: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints "feature/shipping" (line 20) and "main" (line 25) right after each switch.

outputs/stage-0/scripts/git/branches.txt at tag stage-0, lines 1-4: "  feature/currency 2f97b1c ...", "  feature/shipping 59f8ec8 ...", "* main             57a2d53 [origin/main] Add a README"; lines 32-33 both read "57a2d53 Add a README". Only main carries square brackets.

Output lines 21-24: prices.txt, shipping.sh, test.sh, total.sh; lines 26-29: README.md, prices.txt, test.sh, total.sh.

'Add a second product'` come `git branch feature/shipping` and `git branch feature/currency`, then three saves — 'Round the total down to millions', 'Explain the rounding', 'Add a README' — before any switch. `save()` is defined at lines 20-24: it exports GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE from $1, `git add -A`, `git commit --message "$2"`. Output lines 11-15 give b3472f6, c812dbd, 57a2d53 above 09c8526.

The captured --graph listing draws three columns collapsing into 09c8526 with `|/` at lines 10 and 14: 2f97b1c, 1108382 (below 59f8ec8) and b3472f6 (below c812dbd and 57a2d53) each sit directly on 09c8526, which is the last commit shown before d915e63. build-history.sh confirms the two `git branch` lines were run while main stood at that commit.

Opinion claim, and the lesson states it only in the conditioned form "two steps, and the second is where care is needed" (section 9) — no unconditional recommendation, no comparative ranking, no always/never. Nothing to source.

gitglossary(7) 2.46, working tree: "The tree of actual checked out files. The working tree normally contains the contents of the HEAD commit's tree, plus any local changes that you have made but not yet committed." The lesson's "working directory" is a naming choice carried over from the previous lesson; no technical consequence.

git-remote(1) 2.46, set-head: "Sets or deletes the default branch (i.e. the target of the symbolic-ref refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD) for the named remote." So the definition holds. But the causal half fails: nothing in git-remote(1) or git-fetch(1) 2.46 documents a plain `git remote add` + `git fetch` creating refs/remotes/origin/HEAD (only `remote add -m`, `remote set-head`, or `git clone` are documented to set it), so the origin/HEAD line in the captured graph is not explained by the pinned version's documentation.
claim_verdicts.source: git-remote.html:534-535,565-573; git-fetch.html (no mention of refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD) (Git 2.46 manual)
claim_verdicts.suggested_text: `origin/HEAD` is a symbolic name whose target is the remote's default branch; the Git in the lab box sets it while fetching, so it appears beside `origin/main` in this listing.

claim_verdicts.evidence: git-switch(1) shipped with Git for Windows v2.46.0 ends its description with: "THIS COMMAND IS EXPERIMENTAL. THE BEHAVIOR MAY CHANGE." git-checkout(1) 2.46 DESCRIPTION: "Updates files in the working tree to match the version in the index or the specified tree. If no pathspec was given, git checkout will also update HEAD to set the specified branch as the current branch." Version confirmed by ReleaseNotes.html heading "Git for Windows v2.46.0 Release Notes".

issues.text: Unlisted claim, and false for the run being described. The reader is told to run `scripts/git/branches.sh`; that script's first working line is `/repo/git-playground/build-history.sh`, which sets `origin="${repo}-origin"` and runs `git clone --quiet --bare "$repo" "$origin"` — a second folder holding a second repository is made during exactly this run. Only the two `git switch` calls make no second folder. The sentence as written is not in the claims ledger either.
issues.quote: Nothing was downloaded and no second folder was made; it is the same folder on disk the whole time.
issues.fix: Scope the sentence to switching: "The switch downloaded nothing and copied no folder; it is the same folder on disk the whole time." (Section 5 already tells the reader that the script builds a second repository to play the server.)

issues.text: `git branch -vv` lists local branches only; the `origin/*` names visible in the graph two lines below are absent from that listing, which is the obvious question a reader asks. git-branch(1) 2.46: "Option -r causes the remote-tracking branches to be listed, and option -a shows both local and remote branches." Claim 12 in the ledger says "per local branch"; the lesson text dropped the word.
issues.quote: `git branch -vv` prints one line per branch
issues.fix: Write "`git branch -vv` prints one line per branch you made — the `origin/*` names need `-r` and are not in this listing".

issues.text: `origin/HEAD` appears in the captured graph although the script runs only `git remote add origin` and `git fetch --quiet origin`. Git 2.46 (the pinned version, versions.yaml git: "2.46") documents refs/remotes/<name>/HEAD as being set by `git remote add -m`, `git remote set-head` or `git clone` — not by a plain fetch. The lab box installs Alpine's `git` unpinned (lab/Dockerfile: `apk add --no-cache ... git`), so this line of output comes from a Git whose version is not the pinned one and whose behaviour differs here.
issues.quote: `origin/HEAD` is the name that records which branch that second repository starts on
issues.fix: Either drop the `origin/HEAD` clause, or attribute it: "`origin/HEAD` is a symbolic name pointing at the remote's default branch; the Git in the lab box sets it when it fetches." Separately, pin the lab box's git version in lab/Dockerfile so captured output matches versions.yaml.

issues.text: Unlisted claim about the example system. `scripts/up.sh` runs `./scripts/dev-secrets.sh` and `docker compose up -d --build --wait`: a second run rebuilds the images and re-waits, so "changes nothing" is true of the end state but not of what the command does, and the reader may watch a long rebuild wondering whether they broke something.
